result.verdict: SCOPE-(a) NEGATIVE with a POSITIVE facet. Seminormal reps validated (Hecke+braid+Σdim²=120). (+) The chiral T(2,5) character DOES produce negative signs (λ∈[[4, 1], [2, 1, 1, 1]]) -- something every positive/KL ansatz structurally CANNOT (SelectionRules.nonneg_sum_ne_neg_target). So the chirality selection rule is confirmed: the parity-allowed T(2,odd) class is genuinely capable of the mixed sign. (−) But the RAW T(2,5) character is not the exact Δ_λ sign map (4/7 mismatch, incl. two degenerate zeros at the [3,2]/[2,2,1] conjugate pair). The exact chiral combiner is elsewhere. FRAMING PRUNE (formalize-first): re-framing does NOT help -- the ribbon twist θ_λ=q^{2(n(λ')-n(λ))} is >0 at real q_0, so every writhe/framing power θ_λ^{-w} is a positive scalar and preserves the sign; the 4/7 mismatch is framing-invariant at real q_0. The target sgn(Δ_λ)=sgn(w_0^{S_{λ'}})=(-1)^{n(λ)} is exactly the sign of θ_λ at a ROOT OF UNITY (where the twist can be negative) -- a FIBRE / Im(q)≠0 signature, NOT an archimedean real-q>0 quantity. So the chirality lives at the fibre level (mirroring the c_3 fibre-vs-archimedean split, AGENTS.md Im(q) banner): the genuine next probe is the chiral character at q=root of unity, not a real-q re-framing. Prunes bare-cinquefoil AND the real-q re-framing; keeps the selection rule + relocates the sign to the fibre. NOTHING wired.
